5.7.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is any effort aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is any activity to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the area of Garut Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and the community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social function properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children in a gender-sensitive manner. 30.

Article 3

The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.

(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been deprived of their education; and
d. fostering and improving the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, even though according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 14

(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 10 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.

(2) In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may transfer to the Regional Government and other family members to be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11

(1) The Regional Government as referred to in Article 10 letter a, is obliged and responsible to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to regional financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government formulates programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

Article 17

Services as referred to in Article 15 letter b, take into account: a. service principles; and

b. forms of services for victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is any effort aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is any activity to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the area of Garut Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and the community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social function properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children in a gender-sensitive manner. 30.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is any effort aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is any activity to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the area of Garut Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and the community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social function properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children in a gender-sensitive manner. 30.

Article 3

The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.

(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been deprived of their education; and
d. fostering and improving the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11

(1) The Regional Government as referred to in Article 10 letter a, is obliged and responsible to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to regional financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government formulates programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).

Article 41

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection and fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force, the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit, and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 31

To assist in the protection of women and children, the Regional Government may establish:

a. P2TP2A at the Regional level;
b. Women and Children Protection Task Force at the Sub-district Level; c. Women and Children Protection Unit at the Village/Sub-district Level; and
d. Other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, even though according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 17. CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, even though according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 41

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection and fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force, the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit, and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 3

The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 12

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 10 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to village financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government formulates programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the Village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.

(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been deprived of their education; and
d. fostering and improving the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 39

(1) Reporting on the implementation of protection for women and children from violence is conducted by:

a. P2TP2A to the Regent;
b. the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force to the Sub-District Head; and
c. the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit to the Village Head/Sub-Village Head.
(2) The reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) The submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted at least once every 3 (three) months.

Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the Government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, Integrated Crisis Center (PKT), Integrated Service Center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women's crisis center, training center, Science and Technology Information Center (PIPTEK), safe house (shelter), shelter house, or other forms. 31. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a functional Work Unit that provides protection services and integrated handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Sub-district level. 32. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a functional Work Unit that provides protection services and integrated handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Village/Sub-district level.

Article 40

Funding for the protection of women and children is sourced from:

a. APBD;
b. APBDes; and
c. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:

a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal duties and functions in the field of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

b. Women and Children Protection Task Force at the Sub-district Level; c. Women and Children Protection Unit at the Village/Sub-district Level; and
d. Other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 10 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services for victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to village financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government formulates programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the Village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 3

The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 41

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection and fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force, the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit, and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 40

Funding for the protection of women and children is sourced from:

a. APBD;
b. APBDes; and
c. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 14

(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 10 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.

(2) In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may transfer to the Regional Government and other family members to be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.

(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been deprived of their education; and
d. fostering and improving the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:

a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal duties and functions in the field of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 31

d. Other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, even though according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 41

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection and fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force, the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit, and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is any effort aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is any activity to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the area of Garut Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and the community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social function properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children in a gender-sensitive manner. 30.

Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social function properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children in a gender-sensitive manner. 30.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 41

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection and fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force, the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit, and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 22

Health services as referred to in Article 19 letter a number 3 include:

a. first aid to victims by competent officers;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services as needed.

Article 17

Services as referred to in Article 15 letter b, take into account: a. service principles; and

b. forms of services for victims.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 3

The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, even though according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 26

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:

a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal duties and functions in the field of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.

(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been deprived of their education; and
d. fostering and improving the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government formulates programs and action activities for the protection of women and children in the Village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.

(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been deprived of their education; and
d. fostering and improving the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13

(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c is obligated and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. preventing acts of violence against women and children;

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and

c. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes the death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to meet the reasonable needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, even though according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, pictures, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something against their own will.

Article 41

(1) Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of organizing protection and fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force, the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit, and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 39

(1) Reporting on the implementation of protection for women and children from violence is conducted by:

a. P2TP2A to the Regent;
b. the Sub-District Level Women and Child Protection Task Force to the Sub-District Head; and
c. the Village/Sub-Village Level Women and Child Protection Task Unit to the Village Head/Sub-Village Head.
(2) The reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) The submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is any effort aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is any activity to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or step mother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Society is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the area of Garut Regency. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and the community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social function properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children in a gender-sensitive manner. 30.
